outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no source I could read states that the Birch–Tate equality is settled for all totally real fields; the 2-primary part for non-abelian totally real fields is the open piece in every source I opened. In the window: a conjectural homological reformulation (Amorim, Picinini, Ramos, Verissimo; arXiv 2609.28677, 23 Sep 2026); a Lean blueprint checkpoint (GitHub PR #3912, 29 Sep 2026) whose Birch–Tate node for every totally real field is marked planned, not proved; an EMS book chapter by Kurihara (2025) that, per its abstract, claims the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture including p=2 for CM-fields but does not name Birch–Tate; and Elmanto–Zhang (6 May 2024), a generalisation whose authors keep a possible power-of-2 caveat for non-abelian totally real fields. The odd part and the 2-part for abelian fields predate the window (Wiles 1990, relayed; Mazur–Wiles, not opened). The route that could in principle settle the 2-part (Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang's p=2 Ribet-lemma work, arXiv 2310.16396, plus Kolster 1989) is stated in the arXiv text only as an expected consequence.
problem_asks: The bullet asks about the centre of the Steinberg group of the ring of integers O_F of a number field F (the tame kernel K₂(O_F), a finite group), and asks for its order to be related to the Dedekind zeta function ζ_F. Part by part: (1) for each number field F in the scope, the order of K₂(O_F); (2) the value ζ_F, specifically at s = −1 in the form the name refers to; (3) the relation between them, as an equality, which the bullet does not write down. The bullet gives no constant, no w₂(F), no sign, and does not restrict to totally real fields. The formula the linked article and the literature attach to the name is #K₂(O_F) = |w₂(F)·ζ_F(−1)| for totally real F, with w₂(F) the largest N such that Q(μ_N) over F has elementary abelian 2-group Galois group. I take that totally real form as the content of the bullet, because the bullet's own wording (‘relation … to the field’s Dedekind zeta function’) is loose and the article states the formula only for totally real fields. If the bullet is read for all number fields, a second part is asked: a formula for fields with complex places, which none of the sources I read gives. Within the totally real formula there are two parts to settle: the odd part (prime-to-2 order) and the 2-primary part. The bullet asks for the relation, not a proof or refutation of any analogue. Results on abelian fields only, on the odd part only, on Artin L-functions, on tori, on S-integers, or in a homological form are analogues or partial cases of this question.

events.what_happened: Karl Friedrich Hettling, ‘On K₂ of Rings of Integers of Totally Real Number Fields’, LSU PhD dissertation (57 pp.). Per the repository landing page: the 2-part of the Birch–Tate conjecture holds for any totally real field, not necessarily abelian, that satisfies one of two divisibility conditions, which the abstract says are equivalent using results of Hurrelbrink, Conner and K. S. Brown. The extracted text garbles the conditions. Only the landing page was read; the PDF was not.
events.delivers: The 2-primary part of the totally real Birch–Tate equality for totally real F satisfying the stated divisibility condition (equivalently, per the abstract, the other condition). Covers non-abelian F in that class.
events.remains: The 2-primary part for totally real fields outside that condition. The odd part is not its concern.

checked_by.who: LSU doctoral committee (not named on the landing page)
checked_by.qualification: Approval of a PhD dissertation in mathematics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the thesis; inferred from the degree award, not verified from the committee page

events.doubts: The non-abelian scope depends on a divisibility condition whose exact form I could not read, and on Hurrelbrink and Conner results I did not open.
events.direction: Consistent with the equality; confirms the 2-part in a restricted class of non-abelian totally real fields.

events.what_happened: Manfred Kolster, ‘A Relation Between the 2-Primary Parts of the Main Conjecture and the Birch–Tate Conjecture’, Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 32(2) (1989) 248–251, DOI 10.4153/CMB-1989-036-8. The abstract as read begins: ‘It is shown that for totally real number fields the Main Conjecture in Iwasawa-Theory for p = 2 proposed by Fédérer implies’; the fetch report gives the rest as the 2-primary part of Birch–Tate. A search summary of the same page (not confirmed by my reading) adds that the 2-primary part holds whenever the 2-Sylow subgroup of K₂(O) is elementary abelian. The same literature describes Fédérer’s p=2 analogue as still open as of 1989.
events.revisions: Published online 20 Nov 2018 per the Cambridge page; issue dated 1 June 1989.
events.delivers: Conditional: Fédérer’s Main Conjecture at p = 2 for totally real F implies the 2-primary part of Birch–Tate for F. No unconditional 2-part.
events.remains: The 2-primary part for every totally real F, unless Fédérer’s conjecture is established. The odd part is outside it.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper; referee identities not on the page

events.direction: Ties the 2-part to a Main Conjecture at p = 2; gives no direction on the equality itself.

events.what_happened: Andrew Wiles, ‘The Iwasawa conjecture for totally real fields’, Annals of Mathematics 131 (1990) 493–540, as cited in the Encyclopedia of Mathematics entry on Birch–Tate. The encyclopedia entry could not be fetched (HTTP 502 on every attempt), and the Wiles paper was not opened. The statement below is relayed from search summaries of that entry: Birch–Tate holds up to a power of 2 for every totally real F, and exactly when F is abelian over Q. The abelian case is credited earlier to Mazur and Wiles (not opened).
events.delivers: Birch–Tate up to a power of 2 for every totally real F; exact for totally real abelian F (as relayed).
events.remains: The power-of-2 factor for non-abelian totally real F, which is the 2-part question.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published; I did not verify the publication record

events.direction: Confirms the equality up to a power of 2 for all totally real fields; exact for abelian ones (as relayed).

events.what_happened: Jonathan W. Sands and Lloyd D. Simons, ‘Values at s=−1 of L-functions for multiquadratic extensions of number fields, and annihilation of the tame kernel’, arXiv math/0606139 (6 June 2006; 15 pp.; no journal reference on the arXiv page). Assumes Birch–Tate for each relative quadratic subextension and for the base field. Shows that K₂ of the ring of integers of the compositum is annihilated by a generalised Stickelberger element, excluding one rare situation; the odd-part annihilation is unconditional. The abstract calls Birch–Tate ‘almost fully established’ in 2006.
events.delivers: Conditional annihilation of K₂(O) by a Stickelberger-type element, given Birch–Tate for the subfields and base; odd-part version unconditional.
events.remains: Birch–Tate itself: this event takes it as a hypothesis and gives no evaluation of K₂ orders.
events.direction: No direction on the equality; a conditional consequence of it.

events.what_happened: Jonathan W. Sands, ‘Values at s=−1 of L-functions for relative quadratic extensions of number fields, and the Fitting ideal of the tame kernel’, arXiv math/0702346 (13 Feb 2007; 24 pp.; one version; no journal reference on the page). For a relative quadratic extension E/F of totally real fields, assuming the 2-part of Birch–Tate for E and for F, shows the Fitting ideal of K₂ over Z[G] equals a generalised Stickelberger ideal. The equality after tensoring with Z[1/2][G] is unconditional.
events.delivers: A conditional Fitting-ideal identity, given the 2-part of Birch–Tate for E and F; unconditional after inverting 2.
events.remains: The 2-part of Birch–Tate, which is assumed for E and F rather than proved; the 2-integral Fitting ideal statement.
events.direction: No direction on the equality; conditional on its 2-part.

events.what_happened: Takao Yamazaki, ‘Milnor K-group attached to a torus and Birch–Tate conjecture’, arXiv 0804.3260 (21 Apr 2008; one version; no journal reference). Formulates a torus-coefficient conjecture relating the order of Somekawa’s Milnor K-group of a torus T to the value at s = −1 of the Artin L-function of T’s cocharacter group. For T = G_m it reduces to the classical Birch–Tate conjecture. The abstract says the conjecture is proved ‘under a certain assumption’, which it does not identify. A Japanese talk abstract (search summary, not opened) says the 2-power part is handled under a meta-cyclic splitting assumption.
events.delivers: A generalisation to tori and Artin L-functions, recovering the classical case when T = G_m; proved only under an unidentified assumption.
events.remains: The classical Birch–Tate equality for number fields, since this event is an analogue with a conditional proof.
events.direction: Analogue for tori; consistent with the classical form; no direction on the classical equality.

events.what_happened: Li-Tong Deng and Yong-Xiong Li, ‘An application of Birch–Tate formula to tame kernels of real quadratic number fields’, arXiv 2307.05895 (submitted 12 July 2023; one version). For a real quadratic field F with discriminant D, an induction argument on imprimitive Dirichlet L-values gives 2-divisibility of L(χ_F, −1). Using the Birch–Tate formula for F as an input, the authors determine the 2-primary part of K₂O_F for families in which D may have arbitrarily many prime divisors, and give a new proof of a Browkin–Schinzel theorem.
events.delivers: The 2-primary structure of K₂O_F for families of real quadratic fields, using the Birch–Tate formula for those fields as an input.
events.remains: Birch–Tate itself, which the paper uses rather than proves; the 2-part for totally real fields outside the families.
events.direction: Uses the formula; gives no direction on the equality.

events.what_happened: Georges Gras, ‘Genus theory of p-adic pseudo-measures – Tame kernels and abelian p-ramification’, arXiv 2310.10112 (v1 16 Oct 2023; v2 18 Jan 2024, ‘complete reorganization … new results and computations’). Published Acta Arithmetica 218 (2025), DOI 10.4064/aa240130-9-6. Starting from the Birch–Tate formula for real abelian fields, compares for quadratic and cyclic cubic fields with p ∈ {2, 3} the p-parts of #K₂(Z_K) with the torsion group of abelian p-ramification theory. Proves the Deng–Li conjecture on the structure of K₂(Z_K)[2^∞] for a family of real quadratic fields (its Theorem B, not read). PARI programs and tables appear in an appendix.
events.revisions: v2 18 Jan 2024 (before the frozen revision); journal version Acta Arithmetica 218 (2025).
events.delivers: Structure of K₂(Z_K)[2^∞] for a family of real quadratic fields, and p-part comparisons for quadratic and cyclic cubic fields with p = 2, 3. Uses the Birch–Tate formula; does not prove it.
events.remains: Birch–Tate itself, and the 2-part for totally real fields outside the families treated.

checked_by.who: Acta Arithmetica (journal, Polish Academy of Sciences)

events.direction: Uses the formula and compares 2- and 3-parts with another invariant; no direction on the equality itself.

events.what_happened: Samit Dasgupta, Mahesh Kakde, Jesse Silliman, Jiuya Wang, ‘The Residually Indistinguishable Case of Ribet’s Method for GL2’, arXiv 2310.16396 (submitted 25 Oct 2023; revised 26 Oct 2023; 47 pp.; math.NT; no journal reference on the arXiv page). Main theorem: a general version of Ribet’s Lemma for GL2 without the residually-distinguished hypothesis. Introduction (read via ar5iv): ‘Our results should also yield a version of the classical Main Conjecture of Iwasawa Theory over totally real fields at the prime p=2.’ Seminar abstracts from 2023 (Penn, UCSD; search snippets only, not opened) say ‘one obtains a proof of the Iwasawa Main Conjecture for totally real fields at p=2’.
events.revisions: v2 26 Oct 2023. No later arXiv version found; Dasgupta’s Duke publications page lists no entry for this paper.
events.delivers: A Ribet’s-lemma result for GL2 in the residually indistinguishable case. The p=2 consequence for totally real Iwasawa theory is stated as expected (‘should also yield’), not as a theorem in the arXiv text. Birch–Tate is not mentioned.
events.remains: The Iwasawa Main Conjecture at p=2 for totally real fields as a stated and proved theorem, which would feed Kolster’s implication; Birch–Tate itself.
events.doubts: The arXiv text hedges the p=2 consequence. The companion paper (2310.16399) says ‘there does not appear to be a precise statement’ for the p=2 Main Conjecture. The 2023 seminar abstracts claim a proof, but the arXiv text does not carry that claim. The only later use I found is the Kurihara chapter (2025), read only through a search summary, which cites the keystone results. The paper is absent from the published list on the author’s Duke page.
events.direction: No direction on Birch–Tate; it is a tool toward the p=2 Main Conjecture for totally real fields, which the arXiv text does not state as proved.

events.what_happened: Samit Dasgupta, Mahesh Kakde, Jesse Silliman, Jiuya Wang, ‘The Brumer–Stark Conjecture over Z’, arXiv 2310.16399 (25 Oct 2023; one version; 56 pp.). Abstract: ‘In this paper we give a complete proof of the Brumer-Stark conjecture over Z.’ The introduction (read via ar5iv) says the p = 2 case of their Theorem 1.2 is handled here, since the odd case was done in an earlier paper, and that one should also obtain the classical Main Conjecture of Iwasawa Theory over totally real fields at p = 2, ‘though there does not appear to be a precise statement’.
events.delivers: A complete proof of the Brumer–Stark conjecture over Z, including p = 2 as the introduction states. This is a Stark-type annihilation statement for class groups, not Birch–Tate.
events.remains: Birch–Tate; the totally real Iwasawa Main Conjecture at p = 2, which the paper says has no precise statement.
events.direction: Neither for nor against Birch–Tate.

events.what_happened: Samit Dasgupta, ‘On Constructing Extensions of Residually Isomorphic Characters’, arXiv 2310.16631 (25 Oct 2023; one version; 23 pp.). An exposition of the joint DKSW work: a GL2 Ribet-lemma variant in the residually indistinguishable case, with the characters taken equal to trivial and the local conditions set aside. Published in Springer Proceedings in Mathematics and Statistics vol. 527 (January 2026), pp. 75–99, DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-13123-2_4, per the author’s Duke publications page. Its abstract makes no claim about the p=2 Main Conjecture.
events.revisions: Published in Springer PROMS vol. 527, January 2026.
events.delivers: An exposition of the Ribet-lemma variant. No Iwasawa p=2 claim in its abstract and no Birch–Tate content.

checked_by.who: Springer Proceedings in Mathematics & Statistics (volume 527; edited proceedings)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published January 2026; referee practice not shown

events.time_since_posted: about 3 years as a preprint; published January 2026
events.direction: No direction on Birch–Tate.

events.what_happened: Samit Dasgupta, Mahesh Kakde, Jesse Silliman, ‘On The Equivariant Tamagawa Number Conjecture’, arXiv 2312.09849 (15 Dec 2023; one version). Using class field theory, deduces from the strong Brumer–Stark result the minus part of the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture for the Tate motive attached to K/F, integrally with the prime 2 not inverted. The page does not mention the Iwasawa Main Conjecture at p = 2 or Birch–Tate.
events.delivers: The minus part of the ETNC for the Tate motive of K/F, per the abstract. Not Birch–Tate.
events.direction: None on Birch–Tate.

events.what_happened: Elden Elmanto and Ningchuan Zhang, ‘Equivariant algebraic K-theory and Artin L-functions’, arXiv 2405.03578 (submitted 6 May 2024; one version). Generalises the Quillen–Lichtenbaum-type relation between special values of zeta functions and algebraic K-groups to Artin L-functions of Galois representations, over finite, function and totally real fields. Proves it in many cases, integrally, ‘except up to a possible factor of powers of 2 in the non-abelian and totally real number field case’ (authors’ words, as shown on the abstract page). Birch–Tate is not named on the page; a search summary says the Dedekind-zeta case sits inside the statement, which I did not verify in the text.
events.delivers: A generalised Lichtenbaum-type statement for Artin L-functions, proved in many cases. For the Dedekind zeta case the authors keep a possible factor of powers of 2 for non-abelian totally real fields.
events.remains: The power-of-2 factor for non-abelian totally real fields, per the authors’ own caveat; the exact Birch–Tate equality is not restated as settled.
events.direction: A generalisation; not a Birch–Tate resolution, and its own caveat covers non-abelian totally real F.

events.what_happened: Dominik Bullach and Matthew H. L. Honnor, ‘On the refined “Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer type” conjectures of Mazur and Tate’, arXiv 2511.07203 (10 Nov 2025; one version; 74 pp.). Abstract: ‘We prove a substantial part of conjectures of Mazur and Tate that refine the conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer.’ The page does not mention Birch–Tate, K₂ of rings of integers or the 2-part of Birch–Tate.
events.delivers: Part of the Mazur–Tate refinements of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, via the rank-zero component of an equivariant Tamagawa number statement. Not Birch–Tate.
events.direction: Unrelated to Birch–Tate; the name is a near collision.

events.what_happened: Masato Kurihara, ‘On class groups and Iwasawa modules of CM-fields’, EMS Press collected volume (series ecr), pp. 149–183, DOI 10.4171/ECR/20/6. Per the EMS abstract (page read; chapter PDF paywalled and not read): ‘several theorems in the existing literature hold unconditionally’; gives a simple proof of the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture including the case p = 2; computes the Fitting ideal of the minus class group of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of a CM-field unconditionally; treats Fitting ideals of Σ-ramified Iwasawa modules over totally real fields. A search summary of the chapter says the p = 2 proof uses the keystone results of Dasgupta–Kakde (Annals 2023) and of DKSW (arXiv 2310.16399), and that earlier work by Johnston–Nickel assumed p > 2. Birch–Tate and the totally real Fédérer conjecture are not named in the abstract.
events.revisions: EMS page shows a © 2025 footer and a © 2026 footer; the first-appearance year is not established.
events.delivers: Per the abstract, refinements in the CM/equivariant setting, including the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture at p = 2. No Birch–Tate statement in what I read.
events.remains: Birch–Tate. Whether the chapter’s p = 2 result gives Fédérer’s Main Conjecture for totally real fields, which is what Kolster’s implication needs, is not stated in the abstract I read.

checked_by.qualification: Publisher of a collected volume; author Masato Kurihara is a professor at Keio University (per a Keio researcher page snippet)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the chapter; referee practice not shown

events.doubts: The p = 2 route depends on the DKSW keystone, which the arXiv text states only as an expected application. The chapter is paywalled and I did not read its proof. Johnston–Nickel (arXiv 2010.03186; not opened) is said in a search summary to assume p > 2.
events.direction: No direction on Birch–Tate. Claims the equivariant p = 2 main conjecture in the CM setting.

events.what_happened: Li-Tong Deng and Yong-Xiong Li, ‘Iwasawa Invariants of Even K-groups of Rings of Integers in the Z₂-extension over Real Quadratic Number Fields’, arXiv 2603.09176 (submitted 10 Mar 2026; one version). Studies the 2-primary part of even K-groups in the cyclotomic Z₂-extension of a real quadratic field; gives λ, μ invariants and an asymptotic order formula. Applications: the structure of 2-primary tame kernels K₂O_{K_n}(2) for certain fields over Q, and λ, μ, ν for a family of real quadratic fields. The abstract does not mention Birch–Tate.
events.delivers: Iwasawa invariants and 2-primary tame kernel structure in a Z₂-tower over real quadratic fields, for families. No statement comparing K₂ with ζ(−1).
events.direction: Neither for nor against Birch–Tate.

events.what_happened: P. H. Amorim, I. V. Picinini, B. R. Ramos, T. Verissimo, ‘The Schur multiplier of SL₂ and Dedekind zeta-functions over S-integers’, arXiv 2609.28677 (v1 submitted 23 Sep 2026; v2 2 Oct 2026; 18 pp.; no journal reference). Per the abstract page: an exact sequence relating H₂(SL₂(O_{K,S}),Z) to H₂(SL₂(O_{K,T}),Z) for S ⊂ T; relates H₂ to K₂(O_{K,S}) when S is large enough; describes rank and torsion of H₂; and ‘propose[s] a homological version of the Birch-Tate formula (conjecture)’ under these assumptions. A search snippet (not read) states the homological form holds when 2 does not divide |H₁(SL₂(O_{K,S}),Z)|. The search-result title ended ‘and K_2’; the arXiv page title does not.
events.revisions: v2 2 Oct 2026 (content not compared with v1).
events.delivers: A conjectural homological reformulation of the Birch–Tate formula for O_{K,S} under stated assumptions. The abstract presents it as a conjecture, not a theorem.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; the equality is not established by this event.
events.direction: A conjectural analogue for S-integers in homological form; does not cut for or against the equality.

summary:
Sources opened: the Wikipedia article on Birch–Tate (a stub: progress is ‘a consequence of work on Iwasawa theory’, with no dates or authors; the status sentence names the proofs of the ‘main conjecture of Iwasawa theory’ without naming them); the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems (Algebra subsection, bullet worded as in the statement, no status note); SciLag P-240318.2 (status Open, posted 2024-03-18, no solutions, no remarks); the Canadian Mathematical Bulletin page for Kolster 1989; the LSU repository landing page for Hettling 1985; the arXiv abstracts for Sands–Simons, Sands, Yamazaki, Deng–Li (2023 and 2026), Gras, Elmanto–Zhang, Bullach–Honnor, Amorim et al., the three 2023 DKSW-group papers (and ar5iv full text of 2310.16396 and 2310.16399 for the introductions); Dasgupta’s Duke publications pages; the EMS Press abstract for Kurihara’s chapter; the GitHub PR #3912 and its repository page. Not reachable: the Encyclopedia of Mathematics entry (HTTP 502 on every attempt, four tries); the Wiles paper; Kurihara’s chapter PDF (paywalled); the Hettling PDF; the DKSW PDFs (the fetch returned raw binary). The Encyclopedia’s status statements, which carry much of the classical picture, therefore come from search summaries and are not verified by me.

The classical picture, as the sources I could read give it: the equality is established up to a power of 2 for totally real fields (Wiles 1990, relayed), and exactly for abelian fields over Q (Mazur–Wiles and the 2-part via Kolster, relayed). The 2-primary part for general totally real fields rests on Fédérer’s p = 2 Main Conjecture (Kolster 1989: its truth implies the 2-part). Partial 2-part results exist for non-abelian fields (Hettling 1985, a divisibility-condition class). Kolster 1989 is conditional, and Sands (2007) still takes the 2-part as a hypothesis, which fits the picture as of 2007.

In the window (after 26 Jan 2024): (a) Elmanto–Zhang (6 May 2024) generalise to Artin L-functions and keep the caveat ‘except up to a possible factor of powers of 2 in the non-abelian and totally real number field case’, in the authors’ words; (b) Kurihara’s EMS chapter (dated 2025 by its © footer; a 2026 footer also appears) states, per its abstract, a simple proof of the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture including p = 2 for CM-fields, using DK and DKSW keystones, and does not name Birch–Tate in the abstract; (c) GitHub PR #3912 (29 Sep 2026) is a partial Lean/blueprint checkpoint whose nodes ‘birch-tate-all-totally-real’ and ‘federer-conjecture-all-totally-real’ are listed as planned, not done; (d) Amorim et al. (23 Sep 2026) propose a homological Birch–Tate formula as a conjecture; (e) Deng–Li (2026), and Bullach–Honnor (2025), are neighbouring work that does not address the equality.

DKSW (25 Oct 2023) is pre-window but is the link the in-window claims depend on. Its introduction says its results ‘should also yield’ a version of the Main Conjecture at p = 2 for totally real fields; its companion (2310.16399) says ‘there does not appear to be a precise statement’; the 2023 seminar abstracts (search snippets, not opened) say ‘one obtains a proof’. The paper is absent from the published list on Dasgupta’s Duke page, although the Springer exposition (2310.16631, vol. 527, January 2026) is listed.

Close calls. (1) Reading the bullet: I read it as the totally real Birch–Tate formula, because the linked article states only that form. A general number-field reading would also ask about fields with complex places, which none of the sources I read address. (2) Whether Kurihara’s p = 2 result is Fédérer’s totally real Main Conjecture: the abstract is about the equivariant conjecture for CM-fields, and the PR, which is the only source I found that tries to chain it to Birch–Tate, plans the totally-real Fédérer node rather than treating it as done. (3) Whether the 2-part is ‘settled’ in the window: no source I read says so. A reader who chains DKSW (expected p = 2 MC), Kurihara (equivariant p = 2 MC) and Kolster (Fédérer MC implies the 2-part) could say the 2-part follows. I did not find a source that states this chain, and the PR does not treat it as done. (4) Amorim et al. is a conjecture, not a proof of the equality. (5) The AI side: the Lean PR credits Claude Code and ‘Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)’ (quoted from the PR description and commit message as relayed by the fetch tool: ‘Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)’; ‘(Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5)’; ‘Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>’). The PR’s own account describes formalisation scaffolding and planned nodes, not a mathematical contribution to Birch–Tate, so I left ai.systems empty under §5.4 and set none_found false. ‘Claude Code’ is an agent harness; ‘Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)’ is named as the source names it. Verify both quotes against the raw PR page before relying on their wording.

No AI system is credited with the Birch–Tate mathematics anywhere in the sources I found. Searches for OpenAI, GPT, Gemini, DeepMind, AlphaProof, AlphaEvolve, AxiomProver and Aristotle returned no Birch–Tate result. The phrase ‘Birch test’ (a benchmark named after Bryan Birch for AI-driven discovery) is a name collision, not a claim about this conjecture. Also no disputes found.
competing_reading: The strongest case that the 2-part (and so the whole totally real equality) is settled in the window: DKSW (2023) says the p = 2 Main Conjecture for totally real fields is an expected application of their Ribet-lemma result; the 2023 seminar abstracts say ‘one obtains a proof’; Kurihara’s 2025 chapter (per its abstract) gives a simple proof of the equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture including p = 2 using the DK and DKSW keystones; and Kolster (1989) shows that the p = 2 Main Conjecture for totally real fields implies the 2-primary part of Birch–Tate. Chained together, these give the 2-part for all totally real fields in 2025, which would settle the totally real equality. The PR GitHub checkpoint (Sep 2026) points the same way, since it plans a route ‘via Kurihara’ to Birch–Tate for every totally real field. Against this: none of the sources states the chain; the arXiv text of DKSW hedges the p = 2 claim; the Kurihara abstract is about CM-fields and does not name Fédérer’s totally real conjecture; and the PR marks the Fédérer and Birch–Tate nodes as planned, which means its authors did not treat the chain as complete.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of Kurihara’s chapter (paywalled; or an arXiv version) showing whether its p = 2 theorem gives Fédérer’s Main Conjecture for totally real fields, and whether it states the 2-primary Birch–Tate consequence. (2) A journal or arXiv version of DKSW, arXiv 2310.16396, stating the p = 2 Iwasawa Main Conjecture for totally real fields as a theorem; the 2023 seminar abstracts are not enough. (3) The Lean node birch-tate-all-totally-real completed and sorry-free, with its Fédérer dependency closed by a cited theorem. (4) A referee-level or expert note saying whether Kolster’s Fédérer hypothesis (as he states it in 1989) matches the p = 2 statement that has been proved. (5) The Encyclopedia of Mathematics entry, re-read, for its exact status sentence on the 2-part for non-abelian totally real fields, since I could only use search summaries of it. (6) Hettling 1985 PDF, to fix the exact divisibility condition in the non-abelian 2-part class.

judgement.why: None of the post-snapshot events proves the Birch–Tate equality, or any restriction of it. Elmanto–Zhang generalise to Artin L-functions and keep the power-of-2 caveat, so for the Dedekind case they add nothing beyond Wiles. Kurihara's chapter is about the equivariant main conjecture for CM fields and does not state Fédérer's totally real conjecture or Birch–Tate. Bullach–Honnor and Deng–Li 2026 are neighbouring work. Amorim et al. only propose a conjecture. The Lean PR marks its Birch–Tate node as planned. Two events before the snapshot settle cases. Wiles 1990 (Annals, relayed) gives the exact equality for abelian totally real fields and the odd part for all totally real fields. Hettling 1985 gives the 2-part for a class of non-abelian fields, and the approved PhD thesis counts as digested. Neither is whole, because the 2-part for general totally real fields stays open and the statement does not restrict to totally real fields. The conditional reductions (Kolster, Sands, Sands–Simons) and the work that uses the formula as an input (Deng–Li 2023, Gras) are none. The Lean PR credits Claude Code and Claude Opus 5.5, but only for formalisation scaffolding, and ai.systems is empty, so its role is none.
judgement.doubts: The competing reading chains three results: DKSW's expected p=2 main conjecture, Kurihara's p=2 equivariant main conjecture, and Kolster's implication. Together they would give the 2-part in 2025. No source in the record states that chain, so I did not credit it. Wiles 1990 is relayed from search summaries. Hettling's committee is not named.
